requirement: Identify the governing public pair as NCT05421624, Amped-PD: Amplifying Physical Activity Through a Novel Digital Music Therapeutic in Parkinson Disease: the 14-page protocol and separate two-page SAP both dated 12 July 2022; keep the reference SAP annotation-only.

evidence.text: The protocol cover prints the official title, NCT05421624 and Date: July 12, 2022.
The separate SAP cover repeats the official title, NCT05421624 and Date: July 12, 2022.

requirement: Describe a parallel, community-based, two-arm randomized controlled trial comparing Amped-PD with an active-control walking program in 44 community-dwelling adults with mild-to-moderate idiopathic Parkinson disease.

evidence.text: The study-design section defines a parallel community-based 2-arm RCT, enrollment of 44 adults with mild-to-moderate idiopathic PD, and allocation to Amped-PD or Active Control.

requirement: Define the protocol population as community-dwelling adults aged 40-80 years with idiopathic Parkinson disease, Hoehn and Yahr stage 1-3, independent community ambulation for at least 10 minutes and comfortable walking speed at least 0.4 m/s.
acceptable_values: independent ambulation for at least 10 minutes

evidence.text: The protocol states ages 40-80, idiopathic mild-to-moderate PD and independent ambulation, then operationalizes H&Y 1-3, 0.4 m/s and ten-minute walking screens.

notes: The later registry displays a maximum age of 85; the frozen protocol value is retained and the discrepancy requires version review rather than silent substitution.

requirement: Apply the key exclusions for atypical Parkinsonism, materially disturbing freezing, recent falls, MMSE below 24, current physical therapy or regular walking exercise, significant hearing impairment, unsafe cardiac or orthopedic conditions, or inability to walk or use the intervention independently.
acceptable_values: current physical therapy or regular walking

evidence.text: The screening and device-training sections specify these clinical, cognitive, activity, safety and independence exclusions.

requirement: Use balanced block randomization after completion of screening and baseline assessments, and before finalization specify the allocation ratio, sequence-generation method, block sizes or variability, concealment mechanism, assignment roles and protection of outcome-assessor masking without inventing them.

evidence.text: The protocol states balanced block allocation, a list generated before enrollment and disclosure to the researcher only after screening and baseline, but omits sequence, block-size, concealment and role details.

requirement: Define both arms as self-directed community walking for 30 minutes per session, five sessions per week for six weeks; Amped-PD adds the music-adaptive rhythmic-auditory-stimulation device, while Active Control follows the same walking structure without music or RAS.
acceptable_values: no music or RAS in Active Control

evidence.text: The two intervention descriptions give the common 30-minute, five-times-weekly, six-week program and identify the RAS device as the arm difference.

requirement: Schedule outcomes at baseline, the post-assessment after six structured-training weeks, and the final assessment after two additional weeks of unstructured self-managed walking; retain the early-training SAM window as a distinct measurement period rather than a clinical follow-up visit.

evidence.text: The study flow defines baseline, six-week post-assessment, two-week follow-up and separate SAM wear during early training.

requirement: Retain the four outcomes called primary by the reference—moderate-intensity walking minutes, daily steps, stride-time variability and habit strength—and obtain confirmation whether they are co-primary, separately primary, ordered, or exploratory and which follow-up contrast governs success.

evidence.text: The protocol flow and outcome descriptions identify physical activity, gait variability and SRHI measurements without a complete inferential hierarchy.
The SAP calls moderate intensity minutes, daily steps, stride time variability and habit strength all primary outcomes and tests both week-6 and week-8 change.

requirement: Define moderate-intensity activity as daily minutes above 100 steps per minute, derive daily steps from SAM stride counts using the manufacturer conversion, express stride-time variability as 100 times the stride-time standard deviation divided by its mean, and score the 12-item SRHI in the prespecified direction.

evidence.text: The protocol figure/outcome sections identify the four outcomes, explain SRHI and SAM processing, and identify CoV as the gait-variability measure.

requirement: Before finalization, define valid SAM wear day and window rules, aggregation over the 4-11-day wear periods, stride inclusion and artifact rules, gait-test trial and limb aggregation, SRHI item-level missingness and the exact change-score sign for every primary outcome.

evidence.text: The protocol describes wearable outcomes and 4-11 consecutive wear days but does not supply analytic validity, aggregation or missing-item algorithms.

requirement: Define randomized efficacy, intervention-exposed safety and endpoint-evaluable populations, treatment attribution, and handling of participants who fail device training, never start walking, interrupt or restart training, discontinue after a fall, withdraw early or provide only a closing visit.

evidence.text: The protocol permits withdrawal after failed device training, interruption, restarting, discontinuation after falls and optional closing assessments, but neither document defines analysis sets.

requirement: For each retained primary outcome and follow-up, define the Amped-PD-versus-Active-Control estimand: population, outcome and change-score direction, treatment contrast, summary measure, timepoint, and strategies for training interruption, booster or restart, treatment discontinuation, device non-use, rescue or concomitant therapy, missing outcomes and death.

evidence.text: The randomized interventions, interruptions and follow-up are specified, but neither source gives a complete estimand or intercurrent-event strategy.

requirement: For each primary outcome, compare Amped-PD and Active Control on change from baseline separately at week 6 and week 8 using one-way ANOVA when distribution and variance assumptions are met, otherwise Kruskal-Wallis.

evidence.text: The SAP specifies one-way ANOVA or Kruskall-Wallis between groups on week-6 and week-8 change scores for all primary outcomes.

requirement: Implement the two-arm one-way procedure as a direct randomized treatment comparison and report the group effect with a confidence interval and exact estimand-consistent statistic; specify ANOVA effect coding or the Kruskal-Wallis rank effect, ties, exact or asymptotic inference and fallback rather than reporting only an omnibus P value.

evidence.text: The terse SAP names one-way ANOVA or Kruskal-Wallis for the two groups but gives no effect, interval or implementation details.

requirement: Treat repeated-measures ANOVA or Friedman analysis of absolute primary-outcome values within each group, with Bonferroni-adjusted post-hoc comparisons, as supportive longitudinal analysis and not as a replacement for the randomized between-group contrast.

evidence.text: The SAP specifies within-group repeated-measures ANOVA or Friedman analysis with Bonferroni post-hoc correction.

notes: The randomized contrast is the relevant treatment-effect comparison; the reference does not explicitly label its within-group tests supportive.

requirement: For each prespecified secondary outcome, compare groups nonparametrically on change from baseline at week 6 and week 8 using two-sided alpha 0.05, while labeling the analyses according to the final multiplicity hierarchy.

evidence.text: The SAP prescribes nonparametric between-group change-score analyses at weeks 6 and 8 with two-tailed alpha 0.05 for all secondary outcomes.

requirement: Apply Shapiro-Wilk and Levene diagnostics only under a prespecified decision rule that identifies the analyzed residual or change-score scale, threshold, small-sample visual checks and consequences of discordant results; document when the nonparametric fallback is used.

evidence.text: The SAP conditions parametric methods on Shapiro-Wilk normality and Levene homogeneity but gives no diagnostic scale, threshold or decision details.

requirement: Define study-wide multiplicity and a success rule across four primary outcomes, week-6 and week-8 contrasts, secondary outcomes and any post-hoc comparisons; do not treat the SAP's within-group Bonferroni adjustment as controlling the randomized primary family.

evidence.text: The SAP tests four primary outcomes at two follow-ups and many secondary outcomes; Bonferroni is mentioned only for within-group post-hoc comparisons.

requirement: Specify outcome-specific handling for invalid or partially worn SAM periods, missing gait trials, incomplete SRHI items, missing baseline, week-6 or week-8 assessments, interrupted or restarted training and early withdrawal; state the primary missingness assumption and at least one sensitivity analysis for informative dropout.

evidence.text: The design contains multi-day device wear, interruption, withdrawal and repeated visits, but neither source defines missing-data handling.

requirement: Use the prospective target of 44 participants from the protocol and state that the selected PDFs provide no formal power, precision or attrition calculation; do not derive the target from later actual enrollment even though the values coincide.

evidence.text: The study design says We will enroll 44; the 14-page protocol contains no formal sample-size calculation.

requirement: Prespecify whether interruptions of at most two weeks with 100% booster replacement, interruptions over two weeks followed by washout and restart, permanent eligibility loss, device intolerance and participant-selected nonadherence are handled by treatment-policy, hypothetical, while-on-treatment, composite or principal-stratum strategies for each estimand.

evidence.text: The protocol specifies booster replacement, washout/restart, withdrawal and comfortable-pace options but does not map them to analysis strategies.

requirement: Summarize safety by randomized arm and exposure period using exposed-participant denominators, participants with events and event counts, including falls, injuries, dizziness, chest pain, medical or technical session termination, training interruption, withdrawal and device-relatedness; define recurrent-event counting and severity.

evidence.text: The walking procedures define stopping, falls, medical symptoms, weekly adverse-event inquiry and possible discontinuation but no statistical safety summaries.

requirement: Specify arm-wise descriptive summaries for baseline characteristics, all analyzed outcomes, adherence and exposure, including distribution-appropriate centers and spreads, counts and percentages, denominators, minimum and maximum, and no significance testing of randomized baseline balance.
acceptable_values: mean and SD or median and quartiles

evidence.text: The SAP supplies inferential tests but no descriptive-statistics or baseline-table specification.

requirement: Prespecify the secondary endpoint inventory and derivations rather than analyzing an undefined all-secondary set, including 10MWT comfortable and fast speed, 6MWT distance, sensor gait metrics, MDS-UPDRS, SEW-D, GDS, PDQ-39, Mini-BESTest, 5xSTS and usability where applicable.

evidence.text: The assessment battery lists multiple clinical, sensor and self-report measures, while the SAP refers only to all secondary outcomes.

requirement: Before freeze, confirm prerecruitment governance and specify validated software and version, two-sided confidence levels, reproducible coding, model diagnostics, small-sample inference, robust fallback and blinded quality-control procedures; present unresolved choices as questions rather than invented decisions.

evidence.text: The protocol is dated 12 July 2022 and identifies the study, but does not document analysis software or statistical quality control.
The same-dated SAP lists brief tests but no confidence intervals, software, reproducible implementation, small-sample method or quality-control plan.
